subject: Post-demo pricing follow-up: token economics and benchmarking
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Burns <olivia@acme.ai>, Jared Nguyen <jared@acme.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo — token volumes & pricing targets (recap + next steps)

Hi Olivia / Jared —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and the pricing info you asked for on the call so we have everything in one place. I copied Connor (solutions lead) and Rishi (pricing) to help with the next steps.

Call highlights (short):
- Primary use: conversational assistant + summarization for customer support transcripts (multi-turn, avg. 800 tokens/session).
- Expected traffic profile: 250k–1.5M sessions/month across regions (US primary) — ballpark 200M–1B tokens/month.
- SLOs: 200–400ms p95 for responses; some batch/embeddings jobs offline.
- Key asks: unit economics target (what your $/1M tokens should be), estimate for monthly spend, and options for Dedicated vs Hosted to hit those targets.

Pricing ask from Acme: you mentioned targeting roughly $6k–$18k/month initially and an internal target of ~$20/1M tokens for steady-state. We want to propose a few concrete options and show where Redwood stacks up vs OpenAI/Anthropic/other hosts.

Attached: redwood_token_pricing_v2.xlsx (workbook with volume tiers and example TCO).

Next steps / asks:
1) Olivia — confirm the 200M–1B tokens/month estimate (we used the session count above). If you prefer, share a sample week of logs (anonymized) and Connor can run a short projection.
2) Connor/Rishi — can you draft 2 pricing scenarios (Hosted pay-as-you-go + 12mo Dedicated commit) that meet the $/1M target ranges? Include migration path and fallback rules for burst.
3) I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review the scenarios and trade-offs.

If useful, here's the quick benchmarking snapshot I promised during the demo (very high level):
- Redwood Hosted (typical applied list price): $28–35 / 1M tokens at low volume; with our suggested batching/cache + small commit, target $16–22 / 1M at 200M+/month.
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity, 12mo): $9–14 / 1M tokens at high sustained volume (1B tokens+/month) depending on GPU mix and quantization.
- OpenAI (public examples for text-generation models): ~ $30–45 / 1M tokens for similar capability tiers (varies by model and streaming).
- Anthropic (public + partner hosting): ~ $28–40 / 1M tokens.
- Other open-model hosts (self-host/cloud partners): wide spread — $8–50 / 1M depending on ops, utilization, and model licensing (rarely includes saving from prefix/KV caching).

We'll formalize the numbers in the attached workbook and show an example $/1M token waterfall (base inference cost, infra overhead, caching/efficiency delta, support/SLA adders).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: redwood_token_pricing_v2.xlsx (Excel workbook, 4 sheets: assumptions, hosted-tiers, dedicated-commits, tco-calcs)
From: Olivia Burns <olivia@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Nguyen <jared@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo — token volumes & pricing targets (recap + next steps)

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly what we need. A couple clarifications:

- The 250k–1.5M sessions/month is accurate; average tokens per session trend toward 700–900 (we'll send a sample week).
- Budget note: initial POC budget is $15k/month but leadership is aiming to keep steady-state unit cost under $20 / 1M tokens. If Dedicated hits <$12 / 1M at our projected scale, that's compelling for us.
- Can you confirm whether Redwood's hosted price shown assumes our typical batching/caching optimizations or is raw per-token with no efficiency applied?

Also: security/compliance question — if we go Dedicated, can we get separate audit logs and KMS integration? We have a SOC2 checklist item there.

Olivia
VP Product, Acme AI
olivia@acme.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 13:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo — token volumes & pricing targets (recap + next steps)

Putting together two draft scenarios for the follow-up:

1) Hosted pay-as-you-go (fast start) — conservative estimate for Acme volumes (200M tokens/month):
   - Applied price (with typical batching/prefix caching assumptions): $22 / 1M tokens => $4.4k/month.
   - Notes: includes 10% efficiency uplift from KV/prefix cache and 3% discount for sustained usage over 3 months.

2) Dedicated 12mo commit (preferred for predictability):
   - Commit level: 600M tokens/month (fits mid-point of forecast).
   - Effective price range: $11–13 / 1M tokens depending on GPU family and quantization plan.
   - One-time onboarding & baseline monitoring: $10k (professional services) unless included in promotional package.

Benchmarking (quick comparators):
- OpenAI: public pricing examples range $30–40 / 1M depending on model and API features (function calling / streaming can add).
- Anthropic: similar band ~$28–38 / 1M for comparable generation models on partner plans.
- Self-host via cloud partners: infra-only can go as low as $6–10 / 1M if you run extremely optimized stacks at >95% utilization, but ops + engineering burden often offsets that saving.

I'll prepare a slide with the unit-economics waterfall (raw token cost -> infra + ops -> caching uplift -> net $/1M). Connor, can you run a quick sensitivity table for 200M/500M/1B tokens/month mapping to per-1M effective price and monthly spend?

Rishi
Pricing & Strategy, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Burns <olivia@acme.ai>, Jared Nguyen <jared@acme.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo — token volumes & pricing targets (recap + next steps)

Thanks Olivia — great context.

Quick answers:
- The hosted numbers Rishi referenced assume Redwood's production default batching and prefix/KV caching benefits (we model ~8–12% token reduction for multi-turn). We'll call out raw vs net in the follow-up materials.
- Dedicated includes KMS integration and audit log export; we can provide SOC 2 evidence and a sample retention config for your security team.

Next steps:
- Olivia: please drop the anonymized sample week (or S3 link) to the HubSpot thread by EOD Thursday so Connor can run the projections.
- Connor: attach the sensitivity table (200M / 500M / 1B) and the example TCO chart in the next email. Add a row showing effective $/1M with/without caching.
- Rishi: please draft the one-page pricing summary for leadership that highlights the two options and a recommended path (POC on Hosted -> Dedicated commit at 6mo if usage >400M tokens/month).

I'll schedule 30 minutes on Friday to review. If POC budget is $15k/month, the Hosted scenario gives a low-friction proof (we estimate ~680M tokens covered at that spend using the $22 / 1M figure after caching). If you decide to pursue Dedicated and hit the mid-point, your steady-state could be in the $11–13 / 1M range which aligns with your leadership target.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
